edges.description: PPT1 loss disrupts lysosomal nutrient sensing and activates mTORC1, suppressing autophagy in cortical neurons.
PPT1 deficiency misroutes NPC1, leading to lysosomal cholesterol dysregulation, mTORC1 activation, autophagy inhibition, and neuronal injury in CLN1 model systems.
Excessive AKAP5 palmitoylation at Ppt1-deficient synapses sensitizes NFAT signaling and links synaptic trafficking defects to neuroinflammation.

Impaired autophagic clearance of storage material and damaged organelles drives progressive degeneration of cortical, cerebellar, and retinal neurons; restoring autophagy via PI3K/Akt or OSBP inhibition ameliorates neurodegeneration in Cln1-/- mice.
Widespread loss of cerebrocortical and subcortical neurons directly produces generalized progressive cerebral atrophy on neuroimaging.
Early-childhood cerebral neuronal loss and arrest of brain volume growth decelerate cranial growth, resulting in acquired progressive microcephaly.
Progressive neuronal degeneration in early childhood leads to rapid loss of previously acquired psychomotor milestones.
Progressive degeneration of cortical and subcortical motor pathways produces loss of ambulation and voluntary motor skills, culminating in spasticity.
Cerebellar and spinocerebellar circuit neurodegeneration produces progressive gait and limb ataxia across infantile and later-onset CLN1 presentations.
Progressive cortical neurodegeneration causes language loss and cognitive decline across childhood and adult-onset CLN1 forms.
Progressive bulbar and oral-motor neuronal degeneration impairs swallowing and airway protection, frequently necessitating gastrostomy feeding.
Degeneration of inner retinal neurons, photoreceptors, and optic pathways leads to progressive visual failure and blindness.
OSBP-mediated lysosomal cholesterol signaling activates mTORC1 on lysosomal membranes, inhibiting autophagy in Cln1-/- neurons.
Aberrant cortical GluA1 AMPA receptor synaptic scaling and neuroinflammatory signaling promote network hyperexcitability and epileptic seizures.
Cortical synaptic receptor trafficking dysfunction and neuroinflammation contribute to cortical hyperexcitability underlying myoclonus.

evidence.snippet: CLN1 disease (neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis type 1) is a rare, genetic, neurodegenerative lysosomal storage disorder caused by palmitoyl-protein thioesterase 1 (PPT1) enzyme deficiency. Clinical features include developmental delay, psychomotor regression, seizures, ataxia, movement disorders, visual impairment, and early death.

nodes.description: Repurposed combination pharmacotherapy with oral cysteamine bitartrate (Cystagon) and N-acetylcysteine evaluated in an open-label pilot trial (NCT00028262) in children with infantile CLN1 disease. Both nucleophilic, antioxidant small molecules cleave S-acyl thioester linkages non-enzymatically; treatment depleted peripheral leukocyte granular osmiophilic deposits and delayed time to isoelectric EEG, but did not halt progressive brain atrophy, retinal degeneration, or developmental loss.
